key_insight: PrismRestore turns one frozen, all-in-one image restoration model into a compact toolbox of callable restoration actions. It leverages channels that respond differently—but partly overlap—across restoration tasks.
problem_solved: Agentic image restoration must combine operations to address mixed image degradations, but storing multiple specialized restoration networks creates a large model-storage burden.
method: Start with a single frozen, all-in-one restoration model rather than a collection of separate networks.
Use activation and gradient statistics in an offline task-prior search to group channels with similar task-response profiles.
Build a compact bank of callable restoration actions from the shared model; further search details are not available in the provided abstract excerpt.
impact: This approach could reduce the storage burden of restoration toolboxes while supporting agent-driven combinations of restoration operations. The provided excerpt does not report quantitative memory savings or restoration-quality results.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: multiple specialized networks versus one shared model with several callable actions.

paper_title: PrismRestore: A Compact Restoration Toolbox for Agentic Image Restoration
paper_authors: Zhaocheng Yu, Kui Jiang, Jing Cao, Yiang Chen, Xiaocheng Feng
